findings.issue: Scene order is Gift_03_10 'Such useless “gifts”' → 03_20 'take them away' → 03_30 'They call me “Revered.”' → 03_40 '(laughs) Close enough.' 'Close enough' therefore judges the ACCURACY of the title Revered ('near enough to the truth'), which is Egon's mock-modest vanity. تفي بالغرض means 'it serves the purpose' — adequacy of an object, not accuracy of a description — so the joke lands on the wrong target.

'one' is a pro-form for the tribute — the sibling variants under the same node (09_10_Neu 'This is perfectly adequate', 09_10_Neg 'No matter how small') are all reactions to a tribute. The Arabic recasts it as a temporal clause about a PERSON being generous (حين يكون كريمًا, masculine), which moves the compliment from the gift to the giver. Every candidate Arabic antecedent here (جزية، عطيّة، مساهمة) is feminine.
findings.suggested_ar: ولا سيّما إن كانت بهذا الكرم.
